title: Scanning Virgil's hexameters
intro: The opening of the Aeneid in dactylic hexameter: six feet, the first four each a dactyl (long, short, short) or a spondee (long, long), the fifth almost always a dactyl, the sixth two syllables. A syllable is long by nature (a long vowel, marked here with a macron, or a diphthong) or by position (a vowel followed by two consonants); a final vowel or vowel + m before a vowel is elided. The text marks the long vowels that decide the scansion and the consonantal i of Lāvīnja-. Choose a line, mark the feet you think are dactyls, then compare with the scansion below.
